```markdown
# Harbour Museum audio guide

## Intent
A visitor scans a code beside an exhibit and hears a two-minute story about it, in English or Welsh. Volunteers record the stories on their phones and must be able to add or replace one without asking anyone technical. Sixty exhibits today, about ten new stories a year.

## Goals
- Scan a code, and the story starts with one tap. No app to install.
- The visitor picks English or Welsh once. The guide remembers it for the rest of the visit and later visits, and they can switch at any time.
- A volunteer uploads a phone recording for an exhibit and language. It is cleaned up automatically (volume levelled, silence trimmed at start and end) before it goes live.
- Replacing a recording keeps the same code, so printed codes never change.
- Stories sound equally loud one after another.

## Non-goals
- No native app, visitor accounts, or tracking of what visitors listen to.
- No editing tools beyond automatic clean-up. Re-recording is the fix for a bad take.
- No languages beyond English and Welsh for now.

## Anti-goals (failure even if it works)
- A volunteer needs a developer to publish or fix a story.
- A visitor has to choose a language at every exhibit.
- A badly levelled recording goes live without anyone hearing it.

## Constraints
- The museum's site is static pages built with Eleventy, deployed to Netlify. The guide lives on it.
- Recordings come from many different phones, in many formats and loudness levels.
- Volunteers are not technical.

## Approaches
1. **Play uploads as they are.** Simplest, but phone recordings vary widely in loudness, and visitors hear them back to back.
2. **Clean up each upload automatically before it goes live.** Levels volume and trims silence. Needs a processing step.

**Picked: 2**, by the museum, for consistent sound across stories.

## The design

### Visitor side
- Each exhibit has a fixed page, e.g. `/guide/<exhibit-id>/`. Its QR code links there.
- Page shows the exhibit name, a large play button, and a language toggle (English / Cymraeg).
- First visit: the visitor is asked to pick a language before anything else. The choice is stored on their phone (local storage) and reused on every exhibit page.
- If a story isn't recorded in the chosen language yet, the page says so in that language and offers the other one. *(My call.)*

```
  ┌────────────────────────────┐
  │  The Pilot Cutter "Mary"   │
  │                            │
  │          ▶  Play           │
  │         2:04               │
  │                            │
  │   English | Cymraeg        │
  └────────────────────────────┘
```

### Volunteer side
- A sign-in-protected upload page. Volunteer picks the exhibit and language, then uploads straight from their phone (any common phone audio format).
- The recording is cleaned up automatically: loudness levelled to a common target (around −16 LUFS, the usual level for spoken audio on phones), leading and trailing silence trimmed, encoded to a small web-friendly file.
- The volunteer listens to the cleaned version, then presses **Publish**. Nothing goes live without that. *(My call, to meet the anti-goal above.)*
- Publishing replaces any earlier recording for that exhibit and language.
- A volunteer can add a new exhibit (name and id) and print or download its QR code from the same page. *(My call: ten new stories a year means new codes are needed without help.)*

### Units
- **Exhibit pages**: Eleventy templates, one per exhibit, reading the list of exhibits and which recordings exist.
- **Language memory**: a small script on the guide pages; stores and reads the choice.
- **Upload and publish**: the volunteer page plus a server-side endpoint that stores the original, runs clean-up, and holds the result until published.
- **Clean-up**: one step that takes any audio file and returns the levelled, trimmed file. Testable on its own with sample phone recordings.
- **Storage**: original and published audio, outside the git repo.

## Calls I made (the museum can override)
- Stay on Netlify: audio in Netlify Blobs, upload and clean-up in Netlify Functions (background function for clean-up). If ffmpeg doesn't fit Netlify's function size limits, the builder may move only the clean-up step to another host.
- Audio is not stored in git.
- Preview-before-publish, fallback to the other language, and volunteer-made QR codes, as noted above.

## Left to the builder
- Sign-in method for volunteers, exact audio encoding and silence threshold, page styling within the existing site's look, the exhibit list's data format.
```

---

This is project-sized: a visitor-facing guide on your site plus an upload-and-clean-up tool for volunteers. So I'm writing a full design, not a quick note. Override that if you see it differently.

I've drafted it at `specs/harbour-audio-guide.md`. A reviewer is reading it now as if they had to build from it. I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer, and then hand you the finished document to review.

Some calls I've made that you'll want to check when you read it:

- **Preview before publishing.** A volunteer hears the cleaned-up version and presses Publish. Nothing goes live unheard.
- **Missing translation.** If a story isn't recorded in the visitor's language yet, the page says so and offers the other language.
- **New exhibits.** Volunteers can add an exhibit and get its QR code themselves.
- **Hosting.** Everything stays on Netlify alongside your website, with the audio stored outside the website's code.
